evals.prompt: Define writing humanization in 2-3 sentences. Name its primitives and the workflow it follows.
expected_elements: Defines it as prose-quality repair (clear, direct, trustworthy text) while preserving truth and intent — not authorship laundering
Names primitives: AI tells, readability signals, rhythm signals, audience register, evidence specificity
States the repeatable 5-step pass (Tell Scan, Readability Check, Structural Rewrite, Rhythm Pass, Voice Calibration)
Notes the reader, not the detector, is the audience

evals.prompt: Why does the skill order its workflow as remove tells → clarify actors → improve readability → vary rhythm → calibrate tone, rather than jumping straight to tone?
expected_elements: The primitives are addressed in a fixed order so earlier fixes (tells, voice, readability) set up later ones (rhythm, tone)
Structural uniformity is a stronger fingerprint than word choice, so rhythm/structure precede surface polish
Tone calibration is last because it is surface-specific and applies to already-clarified prose
It replaces vague 'make it sound human' with a repeatable, ordered edit pass

evals.prompt: Readability formulas (Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, Reading Ease) — how should they be used, and what is the risk of treating them as optimization targets?
expected_elements: Use formulas to diagnose problems, not as targets to optimize toward
Over-optimizing for a score produces choppy, unnatural prose
Match the formula to the surface (FK grade for general docs, Fog for technical docs, Reading Ease for UI copy)
Names the rough targets and red-flag thresholds

evals.prompt: A paragraph starts six consecutive sentences with 'The dashboard' and every sentence is about the same length. How do you apply the rhythm rules?
expected_elements: Rotate opening words — never start 3+ consecutive sentences with the same word (especially The/This/It/There)
Vary sentence length with a short-long-medium (3-beat) pattern
Mix sentence structures (declarative, compound, conditional, question+answer, fragment)
Monotonous structure is the #1 AI tell; the fix restores natural cadence without padding

evals.prompt: Convert this to active voice and remove hedging: 'In order to ensure that the migration is applied, it is recommended that the connection be checked.' Explain the decision.
expected_elements: Identify the reader as the actor → use the imperative ('Check the connection before applying the migration')
Delete 'in order to ensure' → 'to' / 'before'; delete 'it is recommended that' → direct imperative
Names the actor-knownness decision tree (known actor → name them; reader is actor → imperative)
Result is shorter, direct, and still accurate

evals.prompt: A PM asks the writing-humanizer skill to write a persuasive marketing headline for the pricing page and to restructure the doc into a progressive-disclosure tutorial. Is either in scope? Why?
expected_elements: Persuasive marketing/brand-voice work is copywriting, out of scope
Restructuring into a tutorial / progressive disclosure is documentation architecture, out of scope
Writing-humanizer owns prose-quality humanization (AI-tell removal, rhythm, tone) within prose, not doc structure or persuasion
Offers the in-scope part: humanizing the existing prose form

evals.prompt: Someone says: 'To humanize, just add contractions, slang, and a few typos until the AI-detector score drops.' Correct the mental model.
expected_elements: Gaming a detector treats the detector as the audience; the real audience is the reader
Never insert typos or grammatical errors, or obscure vocabulary just to raise perplexity
Detectors are probabilistic, not proof of authorship; do not promise detector-proof output
Good humanization preserves truth, sharpens specificity, and refuses edits that reduce clarity or honesty

evals.prompt: What checks confirm a piece of prose has been properly humanized?
expected_elements: Zero Tier 1 AI tells remaining; no avoidable passive voice
Average sentence length ~12-18 words; sentence lengths vary; no 3+ consecutive sentences with the same opener
Paragraph length within the per-context limit; tone matches the surface; concrete details over abstract claims
No metacommentary; no claim of detector-proof or human authorship when AI was materially involved
